## Core analysis

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_analyze` | `path: string`<br>`string_limit?: integer = 5000`<br>`include_xrefs?: boolean = false`<br>`include_cfg?: boolean = false`<br>`include_callgraph?: boolean = false` | Produce the full phase 1 JSON report with provenance and evidence. |
| `codevanta_callgraph` | `path: string`<br>`limit_functions?: integer = 1000`<br>`limit_edges?: integer = 5000` | Build an inter-function call graph. Edges come from direct calls only, plus calls through a pointer slot that resolves to a known import (the target node is labelled with the import name) or to a statically known slot whose callee is unknown. Jumps, conditional branches, and unresolved indirect calls produce no edges. The caller of a call site is attributed heuristically to the nearest function candidate at or below the call address in the same section, so caller attribution is not proven. Check 'truncated' and 'warnings' before assuming the graph is complete. |
| `codevanta_cfg` | `path: string`<br>`address?: integer or null`<br>`function?: string or null`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000`<br>`max_blocks?: integer = 500` | Build a heuristic linear-sweep control-flow graph (basic blocks, successors, terminators) for the entry point, an address, or a named function. Block boundaries are heuristic, not proven. |
| `codevanta_decompile` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`backend?: string = "auto"`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000`<br>`max_blocks?: integer = 500` | Decompile one function to C-like text with a pluggable backend. backend='auto' (default) prefers a real decompiler -- Ghidra, then angr -- when one is installed and falls back to the built-in mnemonic-level pseudo-C renderer, listing every skipped backend in 'warnings'; backend='native' always works; backend='angr' and backend='ghidra' are strict and fail with a clear error naming the backend and its install hint (never an ImportError) when that backend is not available. 'backend' reports the provider that actually produced 'text', which differs from the request under 'auto', and 'blocks' is how many basic blocks the text covers. Control flow, argument count and types are inferred from mnemonics, so the text is low-confidence evidence and nothing is executed. Check 'warnings' before relying on a fallback rendering. |
| `codevanta_diff` | `left: string`<br>`right: string`<br>`max_functions?: integer = 5000`<br>`deep?: boolean = false`<br>`semantic?: boolean = false`<br>`threshold?: number = 0.9` | Compare two binaries structurally: functions (matched by address first, then by name after moving), sections, imports and exports. Nothing is executed. With deep=true, address-matched functions are also compared by a normalized-instruction fingerprint; equal digests are shape equality, not byte equality. With semantic=true the functions that address and name matching left unpaired are scored by instruction-shape overlap, and the best pairs reaching threshold (0.0..1.0, default 0.9) are reported as one 'changed' entry carrying 'similarity', so a moved function is no longer a removal plus an addition; that score is shape evidence, not proof of equivalence. The threshold is validated even when semantic is false. Arguments are never coerced: deep and semantic must be real booleans and threshold a real number, so deep=1, semantic=1, threshold=true and threshold='0.9' are rejected and the error names the offending argument. Check 'warnings' before assuming the comparison is complete. |
| `codevanta_disasm` | `path: string`<br>`address?: integer or null`<br>`function?: string or null`<br>`count?: integer = 50` | Disassemble the entry point, a virtual address, or a named function. |
| `codevanta_entropy` | `path: string`<br>`threshold?: number = 7.2`<br>`max_sample_bytes?: integer = 65536` | Per-section Shannon entropy sampled from file bytes with a packing triage hint: sections at or above the threshold (default 7.2 bits/byte) are flagged as possibly packed — a heuristic, not proof. Sections without file bytes carry entropy null with a warning. |
| `codevanta_function_hash` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000` | Return a SHA-256 fingerprint of the normalized instruction shape of the function starting at an address. Numeric literals are masked, so equal digests mean equal mnemonic/operand structure, not byte equality, and different digests are not a semantic difference. 'truncated' means the digest covers only a prefix of the region. |
| `codevanta_functions` | `path: string`<br>`limit?: integer = 200` | List function candidates with detection source and confidence. |
| `codevanta_info` | `path: string` | Load a PE or ELF binary and return format, architecture, sections, imports, exports, and symbols. |
| `codevanta_jump_table` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`mode?: string = "absolute"`<br>`base?: integer or null`<br>`entries?: integer = 256`<br>`executable_only?: boolean = true` | Decode a jump table at an absolute virtual address. mode='absolute' reads consecutive pointer-sized virtual addresses; mode='relative' reads signed 32-bit offsets added to 'base' (required in that mode). Scanning stops at the first slot that is not a usable code target and explains why in 'warnings'; a zero pointer also ends an absolute table. Entries are shape evidence, not proof that a dispatcher indexes the table. |
| `codevanta_similarity` | `path_a: string`<br>`address_a: integer`<br>`path_b: string`<br>`address_b: integer`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000` | Compare two function regions as multisets of normalized instruction shapes and return a 'score' in 0..1 (shared / union token occurrences). Numeric literals, frame offsets and branch targets are masked, so a relocated or recompiled copy usually scores 1.0, while two structurally similar functions can score 1.0 without sharing meaning. The score is shape evidence at MEDIUM confidence, not semantic equivalence: different code can score high and a rewrite can score low. 'warnings' means a side was truncated to the instruction budget, so only prefixes were compared. |
| `codevanta_strings` | `path: string`<br>`min_length?: integer = 4`<br>`limit?: integer = 200` | Extract ASCII and UTF-16LE strings with file offset and mapped virtual address. |
| `codevanta_struct` | `path: string`<br>`address?: integer or null`<br>`function?: string or null`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000`<br>`max_fields?: integer = 64`<br>`include_stack?: boolean = false` | Suggest struct fields for the memory a function accesses around a base register, starting at an address, a named function, or the entry point. Only '[reg]', '[reg + 0xNN]' and '[reg - 0xNN]' operands are read; index/scale/segment forms are skipped. Width comes from the Intel size keyword, direction from the operand position (cmp/test/call/jmp/push are always reads). 'alignment' is the gcd of the absolute non-zero offsets and 'array_groups' lists runs of at least three equally spaced fields; 'truncated' means max_fields dropped offsets. Fields are medium-confidence heuristics from operand shapes, not verified types, and carry no signedness or purpose. |
| `codevanta_xrefs` | `path: string`<br>`limit?: integer = 200`<br>`max_bytes?: integer = 4000000` | List direct call, jump, and conditional-branch cross references from executable sections. Each reference carries evidence; indirect transfers are not resolved. |

## Static analysis

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_bridges` | — | Report which external analysis tool bridges could run on this machine: binwalk, unblob, tshark, wabt (wasm-validate + wasm-objdump), objdump, sigrok-cli, adb, gdb and z3. One capability record per bridge with available/version/reason; every probe is bounded (5s version call, import probe for z3) and never raises for a missing tool. Offline. |
| `codevanta_call_path` | `path: string`<br>`start_addr: integer`<br>`goal_addr: integer`<br>`max_depth?: integer = 8` | BFS the shortest call path between two addresses using the inter-function call graph (same direct-call / resolved-import edges as codevanta_callgraph, bounded to 1000 candidates / 5000 edges). Returns 'path' (address + name per hop), 'length' in call edges and 'found'; missing endpoints or a disconnected graph give found=false, never an error. MEDIUM confidence: caller attribution in the graph is heuristic. |
| `codevanta_capabilities` | `path: string`<br>`extra_rules?: string or null`<br>`string_limit?: integer = 5000` | Detect file-scope capabilities in a binary via bounded rule matching over imports, strings, exports and section names: HTTP/TCP communication, process creation, registry writes, service installs, keylogging, screenshots, reverse-shell and injection candidates, packing hints and more (14 built-in rules; supply extra_rules as a JSON file to extend). Every match lists exactly which features fired and where -- the feature evidence is certain, the capability conclusion is medium confidence. File scope only: no function-level attribution, unlike full capa. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_capability_profile` | `path: string` | Profile a binary against eight fixed capability domains -- network (socket/winsock/curl/reqwest markers), crypto (bcrypt/crypt32/aes/rsa/sha), file_system (fopen/CreateFile/read/write), process (CreateProcess/exec/ptrace), registry (RegOpenKey/RegQueryValue), service (OpenSCManager/StartService), gui (CreateWindow/user32/cairo) and dynamic_loading (dlopen/GetProcAddress/lazy_static). Each domain reports detected plus at most 8 evidence strings and a high/medium confidence; the report carries a deterministic 0-100 overall_risk_score over dangerous domain combinations and a bounded evidence list (&lt;=16). Case-insensitive byte scan, capped at 8 MiB with an honest truncation warning. The markers are certain; the capability conclusion is medium confidence. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_compare` | `a: string`<br>`b: string`<br>`what?: string = "functions"`<br>`max_functions?: integer = 5000`<br>`max_strings?: integer = 2000`<br>`max_changed_sections?: integer = 16`<br>`max_detail_keys?: integer = 32`<br>`max_rows?: integer = 64` | Compare two offline CODEVANTA artifacts. what='functions' or 'strings' diff analyze report payloads (an evidence bundle is unwrapped to its 'report' entry automatically): functions match by name and function_hash fingerprint (shapes, not proof of identity, medium confidence), strings are exact set diffs. what='bundles' diffs evidence bundles by record kind and payload digest membership (exact, high confidence). what='reports' diffs two report payloads structurally by canonical-JSON sha256 per section plus element counts. what='metadata' diffs two binmeta MetadataReport documents by format kind and detail keys. Path-backed kinds take non-JSON files: what='wasm' (two WASM modules: section sets, bounded import/export name diffs, byte-size deltas), what='crash' (two ELF core dumps: signal, faulting module, bounded register deltas, same_crash_site verdict with confidence), what='sessions' (two session DBs: annotation count deltas, addresses only on one side), what='nav' (bookmark/comment/cursor diffs via NavStore), what='firmware' (magic-scan hits appeared/disappeared, heuristic provenance), what='screenshots' (two captured 8-bit PNG screenshots: exact pixel diff with changed-pixel ratio, per-channel mean deltas and an identical/minor/major verdict), what='har' (two HAR captures: entry-count delta, new/removed URL paths, status-code and method histogram diffs), what='sections' (two binaries' section tables: added/removed sections plus size and entropy changes), what='imports' (two binaries' import libraries: added/removed DLLs and function-count changes) and what='bridges' (two bridges_report() JSON snapshots: newly available/unavailable tools, version changes). Offline structure only; nothing is ever executed. |
| `codevanta_coverage` | `obligations_ledger: string`<br>`evidence_bundle: string` | Evaluate obligation coverage (ledger v2): match every obligation's evidence_refs in an obligations ledger against one evidence bundle's entry names (kinds), entry digests and payload record ids, and report a complete/partial/uncovered verdict per obligation plus overall counts. Deterministic ordering, fully offline. |
| `codevanta_dataflow` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000`<br>`max_blocks?: integer = 500` | Recover definition-use chains, constants and reaching definitions for the function at an address: one forward pass over the recursive CFG in which register writes become definitions that kill earlier ones and reads resolve against what is still known. Only provable shapes fold into 'constant_registers' (immediates, rip-relative loads, copies, add/sub/xor of two known values). Honest limits: the pass is a linearization, not a fixpoint -- joins take the highest-addressed predecessor -- so the summary is sound one definition at a time, not a dataflow proof. Undefined reads are reported in 'warnings'. The binary is read, never executed. |
| `codevanta_demangle` | `symbols: array&lt;string&gt;` | Auto-detect the mangling scheme of a bounded batch of symbols and decode them offline with a pure-Python bounded parser: Itanium C++ (_Z..., nested names, args, templates, substitutions), MSVC C++ (?..., free/member functions, common types), Rust legacy (_ZN...17h&lt;hash&gt;E), Rust v0 (_R..., RFC 2603 crate/nested paths) and Swift (_$s... / __T..., best-effort identifiers + entity kind). Undecodable or exotic input is never an error: it returns scheme='unknown' or complete=false with a note naming exactly what was not decoded; results carry evidence. Pure string parsing; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_dwarf` | `path: string`<br>`limit?: integer = 500` | Extract DWARF debug-info functions and named type layouts from an ELF with producer metadata (highest-grade symbol evidence). Requires the optional pyelftools extra: pip install -e ".[dwarf]". |
| `codevanta_emulate` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`initial_registers?: object or null`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000`<br>`stack_size?: integer = 65536` | Emulate one function by bounded offline CPU emulation (unicorn): the image sections are mapped into a private emulator, registers start at the ABI defaults plus caller seeds, and the run ends with an honest stop reason (return/budget/unmapped/unsupported/error), the final register snapshot, recorded memory writes and indirect branch targets. Nothing ever executes on the host. When the optional emulation extra is missing the result says so instead of failing (pip install codevanta[emulation]). |
| `codevanta_gosymbols` | `path: string`<br>`max_functions?: integer = 65536` | Recover function names from a Go binary's embedded pclntab, offline. strip leaves the pclntab behind because the runtime needs it for stack traces; this walks the go1.2 / 1.16 / 1.18+ / 1.20+ layouts (located by section name, then a bounded magic scan) and reports each function's name, address and - from 1.16 on - file and line when the tables carry them. The Go version is an evidence-backed guess; UPX-compressed and garble-obfuscated tables are out of scope. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_graph_subset` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`direction?: enum(callers, callees) = "callers"`<br>`max_depth?: integer = 3` | Collect the bounded call-graph neighbourhood of one address: direction='callers' walks incoming edges towards the callers, 'callees' walks outgoing edges (depth 1..16, default 3). Nodes carry their BFS depth from the root (depth 0) and edges are the graph edges between collected nodes; 'truncated' reports a 10000-node cut. An address without edges in the direction gives an empty subset. MEDIUM confidence, heuristic graph edges. |
| `codevanta_navigate` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`preview?: integer = 32` | Navigate to one address: the containing function (a known size must span it; a size-less function extends to the next one), the nearest previous and next functions, the covering section's name, and a hex byte preview (default 32, max 256 bytes) mapped through the section file offset. MEDIUM confidence: the preview is direct file bytes, the function neighbourhood comes from the heuristic discovery lane. |
| `codevanta_obligations` | `action: string`<br>`ledger: string`<br>`obligation_id?: string or null`<br>`question?: string or null`<br>`required_authority?: string = "parsed"`<br>`required_confidence?: string = "medium"`<br>`required_environment?: string = "host"`<br>`recommended_probes?: array&lt;string&gt; or null`<br>`evidence_refs?: array&lt;string&gt; or null`<br>`note?: string or null`<br>`status?: string or null`<br>`expected_revision?: integer or null` | Manage the obligation ledger (ledger v2): typed records for the evidence an analysis still owes, each with a required authority (parsed/computed/verified), confidence (low/medium/high), environment (host/device/network), recommended probes and evidence refs. action='list' (optionally status-filtered), 'get' (one record with its immutable revision trail), 'add' (question required), 'discharge'/'waive' (close one open id, CAS via expected_revision), 'remove'. Deterministic content ids; the ledger is a JSON payload embeddable in an evidence bundle as its 'obligations' entry. |
| `codevanta_providers` | — | Report decompiler provider availability for this machine: native (always available), ghidra/angr (when importable/configured), jeb (commercial, dex/apk targets only) and hopper (macOS GUI probe). Read-only. |
| `codevanta_pseudo_c` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`max_blocks?: integer = 512`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000` | Emit readable pseudo-C text for one function region by lowering the typed SSA IR: every register definition prints as '&lt;id&gt; = &lt;expr&gt;; reusing the folded expressions (rax.2 = rax.1 + rbx.0;, xor self-clears to 0, lea builds ptr(...)). Control flow is rendered structured where the CFG vocabulary allows -- single-latch while loops from dominance back-edges and if/else diamonds whose arms reconverge at one merge block -- with an honest linear fallback elsewhere: annotated 'if (left == right) { /* taken */ }' lines (signedness via casts), calls note their SSA argument registers and a clipped clobber list, phi joins print as 'id = phi(value @ block N, ...)' statements, and loop boundaries / undefined reads stay honest comments. Deterministic, bounded by max_blocks/max_instructions with truncation flags, medium confidence, offline; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_rizin_functions` | `path: string` | List functions of a binary with batch rizin analysis (rizin -q -c 'aaa; afl'): bounded 256-entry list of address, size and name, junk rows reported as warnings. Requires rizin on PATH - its absence surfaces as a typed error with the install hint and a pointer to the offline `codevanta functions` fallback. |
| `codevanta_sbom` | `paths: array&lt;string&gt;`<br>`max_components?: integer = 2000` | Aggregate CODEVANTA inventories into a deterministic CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM document. Each path is a PE/ELF/Mach-O binary or a JavaScript application directory/.asar archive; components come from JS external packages (versions only when package.json pins them exactly) and binary import libraries. The serial number is derived from the input hashes, there is no timestamp, versions are never guessed, and every component carries its evidence as a property. Bounded by max_components with honest truncation. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_search_bytes` | `path: string`<br>`pattern: string`<br>`mask?: string or null`<br>`start?: integer = 0`<br>`end?: integer or null`<br>`limit?: integer = 64` | Search a file's raw bytes for a hex byte pattern with '??' wildcards (e.g. '8B 44 ?? 24 ?? ??'; whitespace between bytes is ignored). mask optionally overrides per pattern byte: 'x' keeps it, '?' ignores it. start/end bound the scanned window; each hit carries its offset and a hex context of up to 16 bytes on both sides. 'total' counts every match even beyond 'limit' (max 4096), and 'truncated' reports the cut. CERTAIN confidence: direct byte equality over file bytes; files above 64 MiB are rejected. |
| `codevanta_search_procs` | `path: string`<br>`pattern: string`<br>`mode?: enum(literal, regex) = "literal"`<br>`limit?: integer = 100` | Search function names (symbol-table and export names plus the entry point) for a pattern: mode='literal' is a case-sensitive substring test, mode='regex' a re.search per name. Each match carries address, name and best-known size. The match over the inventory is exact, but every name is only as trustworthy as its own discovery evidence - check each binary's function sources. |
| `codevanta_search_strings` | `path: string`<br>`query: string`<br>`mode?: enum(literal, regex) = "literal"`<br>`case_sensitive?: boolean = true`<br>`limit?: integer = 100` | Search the printable strings extracted from a file (ASCII and UTF-16LE runs of &gt;= 4 chars) for a query. mode='literal' is a substring test, mode='regex' applies the query with re.search per string; case_sensitive controls both. Each match carries its file offset, text (capped at 256 chars) and honest length. 'total' counts every match even beyond 'limit' (max 20000). CERTAIN confidence over the extracted strings. |
| `codevanta_ssa` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`max_blocks?: integer = 512`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000` | Build the typed SSA (static single assignment) view of one function region. Every register write becomes a versioned SSA value ('rax.3'); reads bind to the latest definition in walked order, with honest 'undef'/'arg' references when a register was never defined in-region. A call records its Win64/Win32 argument registers as 'call_args' and clobbers the ABI-volatile registers (rbx and friends survive). Loop back-edges mark the target block with loop_boundary=true and a phi_required live-in set -- NO phi functions are constructed in this increment, so values inside a loop body still resolve to the single straight-line version and forward joins read the walked-order value. Optional type hints come from the type-propagation module. Results are medium confidence, bounded by max_blocks/max_instructions with honest truncation flags and warnings, and nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_stackstrings` | `path: string`<br>`addresses?: array&lt;integer&gt; or null`<br>`max_functions?: integer = 16`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 2000`<br>`max_strings?: integer = 32` | Recover stack-constructed strings by bounded offline emulation (FLOSS-style). Each target function's bytes run on a private unicorn CPU -- nothing executes on the host; emulated stack writes are tracked and printable ASCII / UTF-16LE runs in the written span become stackstrings with their function, stack offset, encoding and evidence. Results are medium confidence: the string provably appeared in emulated memory, but emulation is an approximation. Needs the optional emulation extra (pip install codevanta[emulation]); its absence is a typed error. |
| `codevanta_symbolic` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`max_paths?: integer = 64`<br>`max_steps?: integer = 2000` | Explore the paths through a function with the unicorn branch-decision replay. Honest limits: this is a unicorn exploration, not a symbolic executor -- the observed side of a branch is the real emulation result, the other side is forced by rewriting the guarding flag or counter ('seeded') and is assumed feasible, never proven: no path predicate, no constraint solving, no symbolic variables. Values are concrete, x86/x86-64 only, and the optional unicorn extra is required (pip install 'codevanta[emulation]'). The file is read and only ever executed inside the emulator, never on the host. Seeded directions are flagged per path and drop the summary to low confidence; a path is evidence about one concrete run, not a reachability proof. |
| `codevanta_symbolic_solve` | `path: string`<br>`address?: integer or null`<br>`max_paths?: integer = 64`<br>`max_steps?: integer = 2000`<br>`solver_mode?: enum(auto, naive) = "auto"`<br>`timeout_ms?: integer = 1000` | Explore the paths through one function (bounded unicorn replay, mirroring 'codevanta symbolic --json') and, when z3 is importable, check every path's branch constraints with the z3 BitVec solver: infeasible paths are pruned with a warning and survivors carry feasible/model/solver_ms. Every solver call is time- and memory-bounded. |
| `codevanta_triage` | `path: string`<br>`compare?: string or null` | Compute triage hashes for one file, optionally scoring a second against it: sha256, the imphash (MD5 over the lowercase dll.function import list, the Mandiant/VirusTotal convention; refused with a warning for ELF/Mach-O where the loader has no library pairing), and an ssdeep-shaped fuzzy signature (piecewise hashing over the documented block ladder). With 'compare' set, adds a 0-100 fuzzy similarity score. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_types` | `path: string`<br>`address: integer`<br>`abi?: string = "sysv"`<br>`max_instructions?: integer = 256` | Infer the C argument and return types of one function from register use (heuristic type propagation): a bounded window is disassembled at the address and every use of an ABI argument register (dereference, scaled index, arithmetic, copy, compare) becomes a type witness, with the most specific rule winning and the losing observations kept in the evidence note. The return type comes from the last write to rax/eax before the first ret. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_unknowns` | `action: string`<br>`ledger: string`<br>`unknown_id?: string or null`<br>`domain?: string or null`<br>`summary?: string or null`<br>`severity?: string = "medium"`<br>`evidence_refs?: array&lt;string&gt; or null`<br>`note?: string or null`<br>`status?: string or null`<br>`expected_revision?: integer or null` | Manage the residual-unknown ledger: typed records for what an analysis could not decide, with deterministic content ids, severity, open-&gt;resolved lifecycle and evidence references. action='list' returns records (optionally status-filtered), action='open' appends one (domain/summary required, ledger file created when missing), action='resolve' closes one id with an optional note. The ledger is a JSON payload that can be embedded in an evidence bundle as its 'unknowns' entry. |
| `codevanta_vtable` | `path: string`<br>`address?: integer or null`<br>`scan?: boolean = false`<br>`min_slots?: integer = 3`<br>`max_slots?: integer = 256`<br>`max_tables?: integer = 64`<br>`resolve_thunks?: boolean = true` | Discover C++ vtable candidates (runs of consecutive code pointers in data sections) and resolve thunk chains from slot targets — indirect cross-references at medium confidence, clearly labelled as heuristic. |
| `codevanta_yara` | `path: string`<br>`rules_text?: string or null`<br>`rules_path?: string or null`<br>`max_strings?: integer = 200000`<br>`max_matches_per_string?: integer = 64` | Match a bounded subset of real YARA rules against a file. Provide the rules as text or a .yar path. Supported: text strings (nocase / wide), hex strings with ?? nibble wildcards and bounded [n-m] jumps, conditions from and/or/not, $a, #a OP N, filesize OP N and all of / any of / N of; anything else is a typed error naming the rule -- never silently ignored. String hits are certain evidence (offsets recorded); a satisfied rule is a medium-confidence conclusion. Nothing is executed. |

## Dynamic and debug

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_debug` | `path: string`<br>`action?: enum(registers, memory, backtrace, continue, step, next, quit) = "registers"`<br>`break_at?: string or null`<br>`address?: integer or null`<br>`length?: integer = 64`<br>`max_frames?: integer = 20` | Run one LIVE gdb debug session: launch a target under gdb --interpreter=mi2 (this tool executes the target in a debugger it owns - the one exception to CODEVANTA's read-only rule), insert an optional breakpoint (function name or 0x address), perform one action at the stop (registers / memory at an address / backtrace / continue / step / next / quit), then shut the debugger down and verify the exit. Requires gdb on PATH; a machine without it gets a typed error naming the install step, never a traceback. Every result carries an 'evidence' record naming the MI command that produced it and is evidence of one run, not a static property of the binary. |
| `codevanta_debug_close` | `session_id: string` | Close a gdb debug session: remove its session artifacts (script file, raw gdb capture, session directory) and mark the record closed. The stored trace summary stays queryable through codevanta_debug_sessions. An unknown or already-closed session id is a typed error naming the id. |
| `codevanta_debug_sessions` | — | List every registered gdb debug session (at most 8, oldest first) with its id, state (completed or closed), target path and hit count, plus the registry bound. Bounded summary only -- use codevanta_debug_status for the stored trace of one session. |
| `codevanta_debug_start` | `path: string`<br>`addresses: array&lt;integer&gt;`<br>`max_hits?: integer = 64`<br>`timeout?: number = 60.0` | Start a gdb debug session against a local binary and run it to completion: breakpoint addresses (file virtual-address space) are validated, a gdb batch script is generated (hit ceiling max_hits, wall-clock budget timeout), executed once through gdb -batch, and the captured trace is parsed into a summary (hits, backtrace-attributed function coverage, warnings). The session is one gdb invocation -- there is no interactive session -- registered under a deterministic id (dbg-001, dbg-002, ...) with the raw capture persisted for status/close. At most 8 session records are kept; close one before starting more. Requires gdb on PATH; its absence is a typed error. |
| `codevanta_debug_status` | `session_id: string` | Report the lifecycle state and bounded stored trace info of a gdb debug session started with codevanta_debug_start: its state (completed or closed), target path, breakpoint addresses, exit code, hit counts, function coverage, a bounded recent-hits preview and the run warnings. Read-only: nothing is re-run. An unknown session id is a typed error naming the id. |
| `codevanta_frida` | `action: enum(devices, ps, script)`<br>`device_id?: string or null`<br>`pid?: integer or null`<br>`script_path?: string or null`<br>`duration?: number = 10.0` | Live Frida bridge. action='devices' lists Frida devices (frida-ls-devices); action='ps' lists processes, optionally on a named device (frida-ps -D); action='script' attaches to pid and runs script_path for a bounded duration (1..60s, default 10), returning the captured send()/console messages (max 200). Skip-gated on the frida CLI tools and/or the frida Python module - absence surfaces as a typed error with the `pip install frida-tools` install hint. |
| `codevanta_frida_close` | `session_id: string` | Close a Frida session: detach/unload through the frida bridge handle (best-effort, safe for one-shot records), remove its session artifacts (script files, raw message capture, session directory) and mark the record closed. The bounded summary stays queryable through codevanta_frida_sessions. An unknown or already-closed session id is a typed error naming the id. |
| `codevanta_frida_load` | `session_id: string`<br>`source?: string or null`<br>`path?: string or null`<br>`duration?: number = 10.0` | Load one additional script into a live Frida session started with codevanta_frida_start and collect another bounded message slice (duration, 1 .. 60 seconds). The script is given inline (source) or by file (path, at most 64 KiB) and only module-backed sessions accept it: a one-shot session (started through the frida CLI fallback) refuses with a typed 'not supported for this session kind' error, and an unknown or already-closed session id is a typed error naming the id. |
| `codevanta_frida_sessions` | — | List every registered Frida session (at most 8, oldest first) with its id, state (completed or closed), mode, target and message count, plus the registry bound. Bounded summary only -- use codevanta_frida_status for the stored capture of one session. |
| `codevanta_frida_start` | `mode?: string = "attach"`<br>`target?: string = ""`<br>`pid?: integer or null`<br>`script?: string or null`<br>`script_path?: string or null`<br>`device_id?: string or null`<br>`duration?: number = 10.0` | Start a Frida instrumentation session against a local process: attach to a pid or a program name, or spawn a program (resumed after the initial script is loaded). One initial script may be given inline (script) or by file (script_path, at most 64 KiB); the session then collects messages for one bounded observation slice (duration, 1 .. 60 seconds). Honesty: the session is one bounded observation run through the frida bridge -- there is no interactive plumbing. With the frida Python module installed the handle stays live for codevanta_frida_load until codevanta_frida_close; without the module the bridge degrades to one bounded `frida -l &lt;script&gt;` CLI run and the session is a one-shot (script required, further loads refused). Registered under a deterministic id (frida-001, frida-002, ...) with the raw message capture persisted for status/close; at most 8 session records are kept. Requires the frida CLI and/or the frida python bindings; their absence is a typed error naming exactly what is missing. |
| `codevanta_frida_status` | `session_id: string` | Report the lifecycle state and bounded stored capture of a Frida session started with codevanta_frida_start: its state (completed or closed), mode, target, whether it is a live module-backed session or a one-shot CLI run, message counts, a bounded recent-messages preview, run warnings and the availability probe snapshot taken at start. Read-only: nothing is re-run. An unknown session id is a typed error naming the id. |
| `codevanta_lldb_run` | `target: string`<br>`break_at?: string or null`<br>`timeout_s?: number = 30.0` | Run a target under one bounded batch LLDB session (lldb -b): target create, optional breakpoint (function name or 0x address), run, register read, backtrace, quit. Returns the typed stop reason, register values (max 64), frames (max 32) and a bounded raw transcript tail. Requires lldb on PATH - its absence surfaces as a typed error with the install hint. |
| `codevanta_proc_compare` | `left_session_id: string`<br>`right_session_id: string` | Compare two registered proc captures deterministically on their stored bytes: exit-code match, duration delta in milliseconds, per-stream sha256 digest match, and a bounded difflib unified diff (200 lines per stream) for mismatched output, with a verdict of identical, exit-mismatch, output-mismatch, or divergent. SECURITY note: this tool never executes anything -- it reads the two stored records only. Unknown session ids are typed errors naming the id. |
| `codevanta_proc_run` | `command: string`<br>`arguments?: array&lt;string&gt; or null`<br>`working_directory?: string or null`<br>`timeout?: number = 30.0`<br>`env?: object or null`<br>`max_output_bytes?: integer = 1048576` | Run the caller-selected command LOCALLY on this machine as an owned, bounded child process and register the capture under a deterministic id (proc-001, proc-002, ...). SECURITY: this tool EXECUTES the command you pass -- it is dynamic analysis, not static inspection -- so pass only commands you intend to run. The child is spawned in argv form (no shell) with output captured via pipes (no terminal emulation, no PTY): stdout and stderr are kept up to max_output_bytes (1 MiB) per stream with the sha256 of the full raw bytes recorded either way, the wall-clock budget is at most 120 seconds (a timeout is reported honestly as timed_out with the partial output and exit_code null), at most 32 arguments and 16 extra env variables (merged over the inherited environment) are accepted. At most 8 captures are kept; a full registry is a typed error. |
| `codevanta_proc_sessions` | — | List every registered proc capture with its state, bounded by the 8-record registry. Read-only: nothing is re-run. |
| `codevanta_proc_status` | `session_id: string` | Report the stored bounded capture of a registered proc session: the exact argv, exit code, duration, stdout/stderr (with truncation flags and the sha256 of each full raw stream), timed_out state, started/finished timestamps and warnings. Read-only: nothing is re-run. An unknown session id is a typed error naming the id. |
| `codevanta_trace` | `path: string`<br>`trace_path: string`<br>`provider?: enum(auto, gdb, frida) = "auto"`<br>`max_hits?: integer or null` | Replay a saved dynamic-session trace against a binary and map every recorded hit onto the discovered function candidates. 'trace_path' is a capture the generated gdb or Frida script already printed: nothing is launched and no target is executed. 'provider' picks the format; 'auto' detects it from the file and 'provider_resolved' reports the choice, while a capture that cannot be placed, or that contradicts an explicit provider, is an error instead of a guess. The work is bounded (8 MB and 100000 lines read, plus 'max_hits'): 'truncated' means a bound or the session's own limit cut the parse, and malformed lines land in 'warnings' rather than failing the call. Hits outside every candidate stay unattributed. A hit is evidence of one run, not proof that the code always executes. |

## Platform and mobile

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_adb` | `action: enum(devices, props, packages, processes, logcat, pull, push, start, stop, setting)`<br>`device?: string or null`<br>`pid?: integer or null`<br>`count?: integer = 50`<br>`local_path?: string or null`<br>`remote_path?: string or null`<br>`package?: string or null`<br>`namespace?: string or null`<br>`key?: string or null` | Read-only Android device queries over adb: action='devices' lists attached devices/emulators; action='props'/'packages'/'processes'/'setting' inspect the device named by `device`; action='logcat' dumps recent log rows (bounded 200, optional pid/count). Device-mutating actions are limited to the app lifecycle: action='start'/'stop' launch or force-stop `package`, action='pull'/'push' move one bounded file (512 MiB) between `local_path` and `remote_path` with a host-side sha256. Requires adb on PATH - its absence surfaces as a typed error naming the platform-tools install step, never a traceback. Mutating actions (install, screencap, bugreport) are deliberately not exposed. |
| `codevanta_apk_decode` | `apk_path: string`<br>`out_dir: string` | Decode an APK with apktool (--no-src, bounded 120s): decoded AndroidManifest.xml, apktool.yml, bounded res/ file count, smali absence (expected with --no-src) and a bounded shallow walk of the output tree. Requires apktool on PATH; its absence surfaces as a typed error with the install hint and a pointer to the offline 'codevanta metadata' fallback, never a traceback. |
| `codevanta_codesign` | `path: string` | Summarise a Mach-O's embedded code signature (structure only, offline): the LC_CODE_SIGNATURE offset, the SuperBlob slot table (bounded), the code-directory identifier, the entitlements key list (bounded) and a certificate count from the CMS blob. No trust verification - hashes, chains and signatures are never checked. Unsigned files and malformed signatures surface as typed errors, never tracebacks. |
| `codevanta_dex` | `path: string` | Summarise an Android DEX file fully offline and pure Python: the header (magic versions 035/037/038/039) is parsed with the Adler-32 checksum verified (mismatch is a warning, not an error), the SHA-1 signature extracted, and the six index tables (strings/types/protos/fields/methods/classes) bounded at 8192 ids each. The first 512 MUTF-8 strings (128 chars each, U+0000 as 0xC0 0x80) plus up to 256 class descriptors and 256 method samples are kept. Malformed inputs (bad magic, truncated header or tables, files over 64 MiB) are typed errors. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_dialog_decode` | `path: string` | Decode the Win32 UI resources of a PE fully offline and pure Python: DLGTEMPLATE/DLGTEMPLATEEX dialog templates become a bounded widget tree (class, title, control id, style, DLU rect plus an honest pixel approximation of 4 px per x-DLU and 8 px per y-DLU), RT_MENU templates (classic MENUTEMPLATE and MENUEX) become an item tree with ids and text, and RT_STRING blocks yield their effective string ids ((block-1)*16+index). Bounds are reported honestly (64 dialogs, 256 items each, 256 menu items, 512 strings); malformed templates are typed errors; a PE without UI resources is a valid empty result. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_il2cpp` | `path: string` | Parse an IL2CPP global-metadata.dat header: version family, header tables with offset/size, and approximate row counts. Structure only; no readable-name decoding. |
| `codevanta_macho_symbols` | `path: string` | Decode a thin Mach-O's LC_SYMTAB symbol table (nlist_64 entries plus the NUL-terminated string table), pure Python and offline (nothing executed). Bounded and read-only: the symtab offset/size and string-table size straight from the load command, defined symbols (N_SECT/N_ABS) with section, value, external/private flags and name (bounded 128 chars), undefined external symbols (imports) by name, counts, truncation flags (1024 entries walked, 256 kept per list) and HIGH-confidence evidence. Bad magic, a missing LC_SYMTAB, a truncated symtab/string table or a name offset past the string table end are typed errors, never a silent zero. |
| `codevanta_pe_assets` | `path: string`<br>`output_directory: string` | Extract the real visual assets of a PE fully offline and pure Python: RT_GROUP_ICON/RT_ICON, RT_GROUP_CURSOR/RT_CURSOR and RT_BITMAP resources are decoded from their device-independent bitmaps into PNG files written to &lt;output_directory&gt; as &lt;group&gt;_&lt;id&gt;_&lt;w&gt;x&lt;h&gt;.png, with a manifest carrying group name, resource kind, resource id, width, height, bit depth, cursor hotspots, file bytes and sha256 per asset. Bounded at 128 assets (32 entries per group); unsupported DIB variants are skipped with warnings, never crashing; a PE without image resources is a valid empty result. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_ui_preview` | `path: string`<br>`output_directory: string`<br>`assets_manifest_path?: string or null` | Render the Win32 UI resources of a PE as a deterministic HTML preview written to &lt;output_directory&gt;/ui_preview.html, plus a ui_layout.json companion with the full structured decode. The HTML places every dialog item as an absolutely-positioned div (pixel rects are the documented DLU approximation), carries data-id attributes, and nests the menu tree and string table in details blocks. Identical evidence produces byte-identical HTML (no timestamps). Pure stdlib rendering; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_win_click` | `hwnd: integer`<br>`x: integer`<br>`y: integer` | Send ONE REAL mouse click to a live Windows window: the click coordinates are window-relative (x, y added to the window's top-left on screen) and are injected as MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTDOWN/LEFTUP through user32 SendInput after moving the cursor -- this is real input the target application receives, not a simulation. The window is brought to the foreground best-effort first (OS focus rules may refuse; that is reported as a warning, never a crash). On non-Windows hosts this returns available=false with a reason; an unknown hwnd is a typed AnalysisError. Pure stdlib ctypes (user32). |
| `codevanta_win_key` | `hwnd: integer`<br>`key: string` | Bring a live Windows window to the foreground (best-effort) and press one named key by injecting its virtual-key code down/up through user32 SendInput -- REAL input the target application receives, not a simulation. Supported key names: enter, tab, esc, space, backspace, delete, insert, home, end, pageup, pagedown, left, up, right, down and f1..f12; an unknown name is a typed AnalysisError listing them. On non-Windows hosts this returns available=false with a reason; an unknown hwnd is a typed AnalysisError. Pure stdlib ctypes (user32). |
| `codevanta_win_shot` | `hwnd: integer`<br>`output_directory: string` | Capture one window's current appearance as a PNG artifact written to &lt;output_directory&gt;/window_&lt;hwnd&gt;x&lt;width&gt;x&lt;height&gt;.png, verified by round-trip decoding before the file is written; the result carries path, sha256, dimensions and byte count. Captures work best on native Win32 controls (Button/Edit/Static/ComboBox, ...); Electron/Qt/WPF windows still capture pixel-wise but expose fewer widgets to the tree tools. On non-Windows hosts this returns available=false with a reason; an unknown hwnd is a typed AnalysisError. Pure stdlib ctypes (user32/gdi32), deterministic PNG encoder; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_win_tree` | `hwnd: integer` | Observe the live window hierarchy under one hwnd (the accessibility-lite widget tree): hwnd, class name (Button/Edit/Static/ComboBox, ...), title, control id, rect and visible/enabled per node, with children bounded to 512 per node and depth bounded to 8 levels -- every bound hit is reported as a flag, never hidden. This reads native Win32 controls; Electron/Qt/WPF applications draw their own widgets and expose much less via Win32. On non-Windows hosts this returns available=false with a reason; an unknown hwnd is a typed AnalysisError. Pure stdlib ctypes (user32); nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_win_type` | `hwnd: integer`<br>`text: string` | Bring a live Windows window to the foreground (best-effort, per OS focus rules; refusal becomes a warning) and type real text into it: every character is injected as a KEYEVENTF_UNICODE down/up pair through user32 SendInput -- astral characters travel as their UTF-16 surrogate pair. This is REAL input the target application receives, not a simulation; text is capped at 256 characters per call. On non-Windows hosts this returns available=false with a reason; an unknown hwnd is a typed AnalysisError. Pure stdlib ctypes (user32). |
| `codevanta_win_visual_regression` | `hwnd: integer`<br>`steps: array&lt;any&gt;`<br>`reference_png: string`<br>`output_directory: string`<br>`settle_ms?: integer = 250` | The automated visual regression loop for UI verification: drive a live Windows window through a validated step script (click at window-relative coordinates, type text, press named keys, bounded waits -- all REAL input injected through user32 SendInput, not a simulation), settle for repaint, capture the window as a verified PNG artifact written into output_directory, and pixel-diff it against reference_png (identical/minor/major verdict plus changed_ratio). Missing reference file is a typed error raised before any input is sent; the step script is validated whole before the first event, so a refused script never touches the target. Steps cap: 64, text cap: 256 chars, wait cap: 5000 ms. On non-Windows hosts this returns available=false with a reason. Pure stdlib ctypes (user32/gdi32) plus a deterministic PNG encoder and pixel differ. |
| `codevanta_win_windows` | `pid?: integer or null` | List the top-level windows of the running Windows session, bounded to 256 entries, optionally filtered by owning process id. Each entry carries hwnd, pid, title (256-char cap), window class name and visible/enabled flags. Works best on native Win32 applications; Electron/Qt/WPF apps expose less through the Win32 window hierarchy. On non-Windows hosts this returns available=false with a reason instead of failing -- availability is data. Pure stdlib ctypes (user32); nothing is executed in the observed process. |

## Web and JavaScript

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_asar` | `path: string`<br>`extract?: string or null` | List an Electron ASAR archive offline (bounded 512 file entries with honest totals), or with `extract` naming one in-archive entry read that entry (bounded 8 MiB) and report its size and SHA-256. Pure byte parsing; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_electron_audit` | `path: string`<br>`max_files?: integer = 512` | Audit a JavaScript/Electron application for security anti-patterns, offline and pure Python (nothing executed, no Node.js). Runs the static app inventory first, then bounded regex rules over JS and HTML sources: nodeIntegration:true, contextIsolation:false, sandbox:false, webSecurity:false, missing or weak CSP, interpolated exec/spawn commands, caller-chosen IPC channels behind contextBridge, shell.openExternal with non-literal arguments, remote loadURL literals. Each finding carries rule id, severity, confidence, file, line, snippet, recommendation and evidence; literal misconfigurations are certain, shape-based findings are medium. |
| `codevanta_javascript` | `path: string`<br>`max_files?: integer = 512` | Statically inventory a JavaScript/Electron application offline (pure Python, nothing executed). Give it an extracted app directory or an .asar archive and it returns bounded modules, imports (require/import/export-from/dynamic, classified relative/bare/builtin and resolved against the scanned set when possible), package.json facts (name, main, electron version), a heuristic per-file Electron process role (main/renderer/preload/mixed), and ipcMain/ipcRenderer call sites with literal channels paired across sides by exact name. Literal text matches are certain; roles and channel pairs are medium confidence and carry their own evidence. Bounds: file rows, depth, per-file bytes and a whole-scan byte budget, every cap reported through truncated flags and warnings. |
| `codevanta_js_recover` | `bundle_path: string`<br>`out_dir: string`<br>`mode?: enum(minify, unpack) = "minify"` | Recover readable JavaScript from a bundled/minified file with Wakaru: mode='minify' (unminify, readable identifiers) or mode='unpack' (split webpack-style modules). Requires Node.js - install with `npm i -g @wakaru/cli`; unavailability surfaces as a typed error naming that hint. Bounded recovered-entry list; the console transcript is preserved under out_dir. |
| `codevanta_replay_fixture` | `har_path: string`<br>`max_entries?: integer = 500`<br>`max_body_bytes?: integer = 262144` | Normalize a HAR (HTTP Archive) recording into a bounded, deterministic replay fixture: request/response records with bodies as size + sha256 + a 128-byte preview (never inlined), and an endpoint manifest that collapses paths into templates (/api/items/42 -&gt; /api/items/{n}) with counts and status distributions -- the surface an agent could train or test against. The offline half of a replay environment: nothing is served, nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_sourcemap` | `path: string`<br>`line?: integer or null`<br>`column?: integer or null` | Decode a JavaScript source map (v3) fully offline and pure Python: base64-VLQ mappings are decoded into bounded segments (20000 max) and the original sources, names and sourceRoot are summarised with truncation flags and evidence. With line and column (0-based generated position) the nearest mapping at or before that column on that line is traced back to the original file path, line, column and symbol name; a miss is an honest hit=false result, never an error. Malformed maps (bad JSON, version != 3, invalid VLQ, out-of-range indexes) are typed errors. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_unpack` | `path: string`<br>`hashes?: boolean = true` | Build a bounded recursive manifest of an archive in memory (nothing is written to disk): zip and tar (including gz/bz2/xz compressed tars), single-stream gzip/bzip2/xz payloads and cpio newc archives (headers only). Nested archives are followed up to depth 4, with 512 entries per archive and a 64 MiB total byte budget; compression-bomb suspects (declared/compressed ratio over 1000:1) are listed but never read, and oversized streams are truncated honestly rather than slurped. Entries carry path, kind, size and optional sha256 for small leaves. Pure stdlib parsing; nothing is executed or extracted. |
| `codevanta_wasm` | `path: string`<br>`mode?: enum(validate, objdump) = "validate"`<br>`timeout?: number = 30.0`<br>`out_dir?: string or null` | Analyze a WebAssembly module with the wabt toolkit: mode=validate runs wasm-validate and reports the verdict plus parsed error lines (a module that FAILS validation is a result, not a tool failure); mode=objdump runs wasm-objdump -d and returns the section headers and a bounded instruction listing. Needs wabt on PATH (https://github.com/WebAssembly/wabt/releases); its absence is a typed error naming the release page, never a traceback. |
| `codevanta_web_capture` | `path: string` | Summarise a HAR (HTTP Archive) capture offline: entry count, total request time, started-time span, a content-type histogram (max 16 keys), unique hosts (max 32), the first 200 rows (method/url/status/time/content-type/grpc) and per-entry gRPC flags (content-type match or valid 5-byte frame prefix). Pure byte parsing; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_web_inspect` | `endpoint?: string = "http://127.0.0.1:9222"`<br>`target_id?: string or null`<br>`observe_ms?: integer = 2000` | Passively inspect one live Electron/Chromium page over CDP: list the debugger endpoint's targets, pick target_id (or the first page target) and return title, url, bounded resources and console traffic overheard during observe_ms. Skip-gated on endpoint reachability: an unreachable endpoint comes back as {"available": false, "reason": ...} with evidence, not an error. Read-only: only domain enables and navigation/resource queries are sent, never Runtime.evaluate. |

## Firmware, hardware and network

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_dtb` | `path: string`<br>`node?: string or null` | Parse one flattened devicetree blob (DTB) offline: a shallow, bounded walk returning the tree structure and, with `node`, the properties of that top-level node (the root's own properties when omitted). Unknown node names are typed errors. |
| `codevanta_firmware_extract` | `path: string`<br>`out_dir: string`<br>`tool?: enum(binwalk, unblob) = "binwalk"` | Extract a firmware image with binwalk (default) or unblob into out_dir: bounded 120s run, bounded transcript parse (max 64 reported entries) plus a shallow scan of the extraction tree (max 64 paths). Requires the tool on PATH - its absence surfaces as a typed error with the install hint and the offline `codevanta binmeta` magic-scan fallback. |
| `codevanta_net_capture` | `command: string`<br>`arguments: array&lt;string&gt; or null`<br>`capture_seconds: integer`<br>`interface: string`<br>`output_directory: string` | Capture network traffic AROUND a target command: starts a background tshark on the chosen interface (auto-stop after capture_seconds, 1..60), runs the command you pass LOCALLY as an owned bounded subprocess concurrently, then waits for both (bounded join) and summarises the finished pcap offline (frame count and first packet fields) through the tshark bridge. SECURITY: this tool EXECUTES the command you pass and RECORDS this machine's network packets -- dynamic analysis, pass only commands you intend to run. HONESTY: live capture needs administrator privileges and Npcap/WinPcap on Windows; without them tshark may start yet record nothing and the warnings say so. When tshark is not on PATH nothing runs at all and an honest unavailable result is returned. Stage-named warnings (tshark-start, tshark-join, pcap-missing, summary) report every degraded step; the result carries the pcap path, size, sha256, the target's argv/exit code/streams and HIGH-confidence evidence (source net.capture, method tshark-around-run). |
| `codevanta_net_interfaces` | — | List the network interfaces tshark can capture on (tshark -D), each as {number, device, description} and capped at 32 entries. HONESTY: live packet capture additionally requires administrator privileges and Npcap/WinPcap on Windows -- a listed interface does not guarantee packets can be recorded without them. When tshark is not on PATH the tool returns an honest unavailable object (available: false with the install hint) instead of an error. |
| `codevanta_pcap_fields` | `path: string`<br>`fields: string`<br>`display_filter?: string or null`<br>`packet_limit?: integer = 50` | Extract protocol fields from a pcap/pcapng capture with tshark -T fields: comma-separated field names (max 16), optional -Y display filter, packet cap -c (1..100, default 50) and a bounded 100-row parse. Requires tshark on PATH - its absence surfaces as a typed error with the install hint and the offline `codevanta binmeta` structural pcap fallback. |
| `codevanta_signal_sr` | `path: string` | Summarize one sigrok .sr session archive offline: version, sample rate, device, channels, logic-file names and byte sizes, and the annotation count when the archive carries one. ZIP-bomb guarded; the logic data is stat'ed but never inflated. |
| `codevanta_uart_decode` | `path: string`<br>`samplerate_hz: integer`<br>`baud?: integer = 115200`<br>`databits?: integer = 8`<br>`parity?: enum(none, even, odd) = "none"`<br>`stopbits?: integer = 1` | Decode a raw logic-0/1 capture file as UART with the pure-Python decoder-lite (medium confidence by design). One byte per sample: 0 is logic low, anything else high; samplerate_hz must give at least 2 samples per baud bit. Offline; garbage captures decode to few or zero bytes with warnings. |

## Formats and files

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_binmeta` | `path: string` | Auto-detect container formats in one file: WASM, EVM (a labelled heuristic verdict, evm_like), GGUF, safetensors, pcap/pcapng and firmware magics. Offline and read-only; the summary carries an evidence record with source/method/confidence. |
| `codevanta_bplist` | `path: string` | Decode an Apple binary property list (bplist00) fully offline and pure Python: the 8-byte magic, marker-typed object table, big-endian offset table and 32-byte trailer are parsed and the top object is expanded into a bounded JSON-safe tree of dict/array/string/int/real/bool/date/data nodes. Bounds are honest: 4096 objects, 64 nesting levels, 512 entries per collection, 256 characters per string and 64 KiB per data object (larger data becomes a hex preview plus a truncated flag). Malformed files (bad magic, truncated trailer, out-of-range object references, self-referencing cycles, oversize tables) are typed errors. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_certs` | `path: string` | Parse a PE file's certificate table offline with pure Python: WIN_CERTIFICATE entries and the PKCS#7 SignedData structure via a minimal hand-rolled DER walk - signer count, serial numbers (hex), digest/signature algorithm OID names (common SHA-1/256/384/512 RSA/ECDSA map) and signingTime when present in the authenticated attributes. Structural analysis only: no trust-chain verification; issuer names are honestly reported as not decoded. Always available. |
| `codevanta_containers` | `path: string` | Auto-detect container formats in one file, offline and pure Python: WebAssembly module sections, GGUF tensor metadata, safetensors headers, pcap/pcapng capture summaries, EVM bytecode opcodes and a firmware magic sweep over the raw bytes. Formats that do not match stay out of the summary; a file matching nothing is a valid empty detection, never an error. Read-only; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_crash` | `path: string` | Summarise a crash dump file, auto-detecting the format: a Linux ELF core dump or an Apple .ips crash report (the leading magic bytes decide). Offline and read-only: the file is parsed, never executed, and the payload carries the format, the parsed summary fields and an evidence record stating how much of the finding was parse-verified. |
| `codevanta_delayload` | `path: string` | Decode a PE's delay-load import directory (data directory 13), pure Python and offline (nothing executed). Per descriptor: the DLL name, raw grAttrs with named trait bits (dlattrRva and the CFG check bit), the layout version (v1 32-bit or v2 64-bit fields, chosen by the directory size), the IAT/INT RVAs and the bounded IMAGE_IMPORT_BY_NAME import list (hint/name entries walked until NULL; bounded 32 DLLs x 512 imports x 128 name chars, every bound reported). Descriptors without dlattrRva carry bind-time addresses, treated as RVAs with an explicit warning. An absent directory reports delay_load_present:false, not an error; malformed structures raise typed errors. |
| `codevanta_elf_macho` | `path: string` | Deep-parse an ELF's dynamic section or a Mach-O's dylib load commands, auto-detected by magic, pure Python and offline. ELF: DT_NEEDED libraries (bounded 32), DT_RPATH/RUNPATH/SONAME, DT_INIT/FINI addresses and the init/fini pointer arrays (bounded 8). Mach-O: LC_LOAD_DYLIB-family entries (bounded 32) with install name, timestamp, current_version and compatibility_version, plus LC_ID_DYLIB. Malformed structures raise typed errors; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_fs_diff` | `before: string`<br>`after: string` | Diff two filesystem snapshot files (as produced by codevanta_fs_snapshot) and classify every relative path: created (after only), deleted (before only), modified (both sides, fingerprint differs -- content sha256 when both sides hashed it, size fallback flagged size_only) and unchanged (counted only). The verdict is identical when nothing changed, otherwise changed. Every list is bounded (512 entries) with per-list truncation flags while counts report the true totals. Missing, unreadable or malformed snapshot files are typed errors. Pure stdlib; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_fs_snapshot` | `root: string`<br>`output_directory: string` | Snapshot a directory tree recursively, fully offline and pure Python: os.walk (symlinks never followed) records every regular file with its relative POSIX path, size and sha256 (files above 8 MiB are recorded size-only with hashed=false), every directory, and every symlink with its clipped target text. Bounded at 2048 entries and 256 MiB of hashed bytes; overflow is an honest truncated flag plus warnings, never a crash. No timestamps are recorded, so the same tree snapshots to a byte-identical manifest. The manifest is written as fs_snapshot.json into &lt;output_directory&gt; and returned together with the written file's path, byte count and sha256. Missing roots and non-directory roots are typed errors. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_gpu` | `path: string` | Inspect a GPU code container: CUDA fatbin entries with sm_XX arch detection, CUBIN ELF section walk with PTX marker detection, or Clang offload bundle (COB) host/device lines. |
| `codevanta_metadata` | `path: string` | Auto-detect format metadata for a file or directory: APK signing block (v1/v2/v3), Go build info, Rust cargo-auditable, Python .pyc header, Electron fuses, ELF notes, kernel-module .modinfo, or a desktop app layout (Unity, IL2CPP, Unreal, Electron, .NET). |
| `codevanta_pdb` | `path: string`<br>`max_streams?: integer = 256`<br>`max_modules?: integer = 4096` | Read PDB information offline. A .pdb input gets the bounded MSF v7 walk: streams, the info stream's GUID/age/version, named streams and the DBI module list. Any other input is treated as a PE and returns its debug directory's CodeView record -- the PDB path, GUID and age that identify the symbol file. No symbol records, no type info (TPI/IPI), no download, no network, ever. Nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_pe_deep` | `path: string` | Deep-parse a PE's resource section and load config in one call, pure Python and offline (nothing executed). Resources: bounded type tree walk (type/name/language levels), entry list, icon/cursor counts, shallow VS_VERSIONINFO key/value pairs with the VS_FIXEDFILEINFO version, RT_MANIFEST preview and a hex raw preview per type. Load config: TLS callback list (bounded 16), Guard CF function-table count and flag names, DEP policy (NX_COMPAT/ASLR/GuardCF from DllCharacteristics) and SE handler count. Absent directories are reported as present:false, not errors; malformed structures raise typed errors. |
| `codevanta_png_diff` | `left: string`<br>`right: string` | Compare two PNG screenshots pixel by pixel: changed-pixel ratio, per-channel mean absolute delta and a verdict (identical / minor / major) using documented thresholds. Different dimensions short-circuit to major with a warning because no aligned comparison exists. Pure-Python PNG decode; nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_proto_decode` | `path: string`<br>`grpc?: boolean = false` | Decode a protobuf wire-format body file into a structure-only field tree (field numbers, wire types, values: varint int, IEEE-754 float, nested fields or bounded hex). With grpc=true a leading 5-byte gRPC frame prefix is stripped first and reported. MEDIUM confidence: field numbers are semantic-free without the .proto schema. Warnings cover unknown wire types and truncated fields; never raises for message content. |
| `codevanta_rich` | `path: string` | Decode a PE file's Rich header offline (pure Python): recover the XOR key stored right after the Rich marker, walk the @comp.id entry stream backwards to the DanS marker and report each entry's product id (hex), build number and object count, the total object count and a best-effort compiler guess from a table of commonly published product ids (e.g. 'MSVC 14.x link 14.36'); unknown ids stay honest. Bounded to 256 entries. Always available, nothing is executed. |
| `codevanta_sqlite` | `path: string`<br>`table?: string or null` | Introspect a SQLite database strictly read-only through the mode=ro&immutable=1 URI: a bounded table list with row counts, and with `table` that table's columns plus up to 10 sample rows (JSON-safe values). The tool cannot write, create journals or replay a WAL; a present -wal file is reported as ignored. Offline. |

## Rebuild

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_rebuild` | `target: string`<br>`request: string`<br>`mode?: string = "clean-room"`<br>`root?: string or null` | Start a rebuild project: Study → Build → Check → Ready. Studies the target with CODEVANTA's analysis engine (surface-only in clean-room mode, all tools in deep mode), writes craft.json and the capture, and returns the project id. An external coding agent then builds the recreation; use codevanta_rebuild_check to compare it against the original. Nothing is executed, nothing touches the network. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_build` | `project_id: string`<br>`root?: string or null` | Mark a rebuild project as ``building`` and scaffold the ``app/`` directory. Returns the project id, status, suggested stack, directory and the list of files written for the coding agent. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_build_auto` | `project_id: string`<br>`root?: string or null`<br>`max_attempts?: integer = 5` | Run the automated Build → Check → Improve loop. Generates code from study entries, writes it to ``app/``, runs ``codevanta_rebuild_check``, and repeats until identical or ``max_attempts`` is reached. Marks the project ``ready`` on success. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_check` | `project_id: string`<br>`build_path: string`<br>`root?: string or null` | Compare an agent-built recreation against the project's original target and record the check. For binary targets uses CODEVANTA's structural comparison; otherwise compares SHA-256 and size. Returns whether the build is identical and saves the result under checks/. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_check_behavior` | `project_id: string`<br>`build_path: string`<br>`run_original?: boolean = false`<br>`timeout?: integer = 10`<br>`root?: string or null` | Behavior check: run the built recreation and capture its exit code and stdout/stderr. With run_original=true (explicit consent; executes the original binary on this machine) also run the original target and report exit-code match and stdout similarity. Recorded under checks/ with kind 'behavior'. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_generate` | `project_dir: string`<br>`output_directory: string`<br>`language?: string = "python"` | Generate deterministic starter implementation code from a studied rebuild project (the craft.json + capture/ layout written by codevanta_rebuild). Writes into output_directory: app/main.py with a header citing the target and the sha256 evidence digest, one import-surface block per observed API group (kernel32/ws2_32/user32 ... grouped from the capture's imports evidence) and one raise-NotImplementedError stub per group citing the reference count and an example symbol, the deep-mode pseudo-C evidence as app/pseudo_c/*.c when recorded, ui_layout.json plus a deterministic ui.html preview from the dialog-decode capture when present, and checks/behavior_checklist.md with one item per recorded check. Identical inputs produce byte-identical files (no timestamps); work is bounded (32 files, 256 stubs, 2000 lines/file) with honest truncation warnings. Nothing is executed and nothing touches the network. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_improve` | `project_id: string`<br>`hint?: string or null`<br>`root?: string or null` | Request an improvement pass for a rebuild project. Regenerates the code in ``app/`` using the latest study entries, then runs one check. Returns whether the build is now identical. Intended for external coding agents to iterate toward Ready. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_list` | `root?: string or null` | List rebuild projects, most recently updated first. Returns the project id, name, status, mode, target and updated timestamp for each project under the rebuild root. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_ready` | `project_id: string`<br>`root?: string or null` | Mark a rebuild project as ``ready``. Requires the project to be in ``checked`` status and the most recent check to report ``identical: true``. Returns the updated project record. |
| `codevanta_rebuild_show` | `project_id: string`<br>`root?: string or null` | Show one rebuild project's full record: request, status, study entries, checks and inbox. Returns the complete craft.json payload. |

## Sessions and navigation

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_nav` | `action: enum(mark, comment, goto, cursor, bookmarks, comments, history)`<br>`session?: string or null`<br>`address?: integer or string or null`<br>`name?: string or null`<br>`text?: string or null`<br>`db?: string or null` | Read or write one session's navigation state: action='mark' pins a bookmark, 'comment' attaches a note, 'goto' moves the cursor and records the visit, 'cursor' reads it back and 'bookmarks'/'comments'/'history' list the bounded state. Every action needs `session` and the session database path `db`; mark/comment/goto also need `address` (int or 0x-prefixed hex string). A missing session is a typed error with the 'codevanta session save' hint. Offline. |
| `codevanta_nav_providers` | — | Report which external GUI navigation providers (Hopper, Cutter, Ghidra) could attach on this machine: one capability report each with name/available/reason, plus the nav.providers evidence record. The probes never launch anything and never raise; CODEVANTA's own navigation works regardless. Offline. |
| `codevanta_session_list` | `db?: string or null`<br>`limit?: integer = 20` | List persisted analysis sessions, newest first. |
| `codevanta_session_save` | `path: string`<br>`db?: string or null`<br>`notes?: string or null` | Analyze a binary and persist its fingerprint, function count, and string count as a new session in the local SQLite session database. |

## Other

| Tool | Parameters | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `codevanta_js_diff` | `left: string`<br>`right: string`<br>`max_files?: integer = 512` | Diff two builds of one JavaScript/Electron application (static, offline, nothing executed). Both sides are inventoried with the same bounds, then set-diffed: modules by path, imports by (kind, spec), package.json dependency pins by name and version, and IPC channels by literal name -- including a paired channel that lost its renderer or main side in the newer build. Every list is capped at 200 rows with the cut reported; the comparison is a shape measure over two static inventories, so an unchanged module list does not mean unchanged behaviour. |
